thread:
alex-sales: Heads up — AtlasHealth sent a redline requesting a Most-Favored-Customer style clause plus 24 months price protection. They want POC discount to roll into any future pricing and a cap reduction tied to committed qps.

sarah-legal: Can you paste the exact redline? MFN language can be narrow but needs carveouts.

alex-sales: Pasted below from their counsel: 
```
If at any time during the Term Customer obtains from Redwood or any third party a lower price, Redwood shall promptly adjust Customer's pricing to the lower price and provide retroactive credits for the prior 12 months.
```

jordan-ps: FYI POC uses hosted shared infra and a heavily discounted pilot SKU — we should exclude pilot pricing from MFN or it cascades to all customers.

mike-finance: Big risk: open-ended retro credits + long duration = revenue leakage. If we can limit retro to the smaller of 6 months or $X, that helps. Also specify "equivalent capacity/feature set" so cheap pilot SKUs don't apply.

emily-product: Also note that dedicated/reserved pricing is on a different rate card with committed capacity discounts. The clause needs to reference "equivalent commercial offering"; otherwise a cheaper bundle (different features) could trigger.

sarah-legal: Proposed compromise language (draft): 
```
Redwood shall not offer any third party materially lower prices for the same commercial offering, capacity tier, and contract term applicable to Customer. Price protection shall be limited to 12 months following the Effective Date and shall not apply to (a) trial/POC pricing, (b) partner or promotional discounts, or (c) pricing for distinct dedicated/reserved offerings unless explicitly listed. Retroactive credits shall be capped at the lesser of 6 months of invoiced charges or $50,000.
```

katie-sales: That seems reasonable. Customer originally asked for 24 months and full retro credits. Can we get deal desk sign-off on the 12m/6m cap quickly? Need to avoid blocking exec sponsor call next Tues.

mike-finance: I'm +1 on 12m protection w/ retro cap as long as VP Sales ok with $50k cap. If we expect larger ARR (AtlasHealth skews >$2M ARR), we need to scale the cap (e.g., min($50k, 3% of ARR)).

alex-sales: AtlasHealth expected first-year ARR is ~$320k in year one for POC->prod ramp. $50k cap seems safe.

sarah-legal: Also want audit right and a clause that MFN only applies to publicly available price lists or signed agreements — not private custom deals, unless the customer provides evidence.

emily-product: Important: If we accept MFN across hosted vs dedicated, implementation complexity increases. Routing, model variants, and quantization tiers change unit economics. We should explicitly limit MFN to the same deployment model.

jordan-ps: For the POC: propose this operational approach — mark POC invoices as "POC — excl. MFN" and include a one-line clause in the SOW. Keeps sales momentum and avoids whack-a-mole.

katie-sales: I'll propose the 12m/6m cap + exclusions + deployment-model carveout to Atlas and ask for redline from their counsel. If they push back, we escalate to VP Sales.

mike-finance: Deal desk: please confirm approval for $50k cap for this opportunity; if Atlas pushes compressed pricing (below our committed tier), we need pre-approved exceptions.

sarah-legal: I'll prepare a final redline with the small edits (audit language + survival) and post it here within the hour.

alex-sales: Thanks — also FYI security questionnaire is pending. They flagged SOC2 sections and a custom data residency ask. That could be another blocker for Dedicated option — sharing in case product/legal need to coordinate.

emily-product: Noted. If data residency required -> private deployment, pricing/commits change. Keep me in the loop.

katie-sales: Copy. I'll update Atlas timeline to push exec call while we resolve MFN language and secQ.

sarah-legal: Draft posted. Short checklist for sign-off: 1) finance confirms cap threshold, 2) product confirms deployment carveout wording, 3) sales confirms POC exclusion mechanics. Once all 3 green, legal will accept.

mike-finance: Green from finance for $50k cap given current ARR estimate. If ARR updates >$1M, re-evaluate.

alex-sales: Great. I'll coordinate with Atlas and share any counter-redlines as they come. :thumbsup:
